hypothesis: Phase-1 spectral OOD failure is primarily a transition-law extrapolation failure, not insufficient information in the frozen 256-token state representation. A structured local operator with a latent propagation-speed parameter inferred only from quantized context should recover OOD generalization.

method.input: decoded physical state from the frozen discrete tokens only
method.operator_family: periodic isotropic second-order wave update using the same local discrete Laplacian family as the simulator
method.latent_parameter: one scalar wave speed c per sequence
method.inference: grid-search c by minimizing one-step state MSE over the two observed context transitions
method.rollout: recursive; every predicted state is requantized into the same 256-token vocabulary before the next step

frozen_pass_rule: PASS only if every one of the 3 fresh confirmatory replicates has requantized rollout MSE ratio < 1.0 versus raw-state persistence on ID h8, spectrum-OOD h3, and combined-OOD h3. No reruns/retries of a failed replicate. Parameter-estimation diagnostics are secondary and cannot rescue a primary-gate failure.
claim_limit: A pass would show that the frozen discrete state can support OOD prediction when paired with a known operator family and inferred latent parameter. It is not evidence of discovering an unknown law, because the operator family is supplied.
